Rashi on Eruvin 41b:10:1.hebrew: לנמל - פורט"ו בלע"ז, ששם הספינות יוצאות מן הים לשפתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:10:1.english: To the port - Port in Old French, where ships go out from the sea to its shore.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:10:2.hebrew: מה אנו לירד - מן הספינה לתוך העיר. כלומר: באנו מחוץ לתחום משחשיכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:10:2.english: What [is the ruling for] us to disembark - From the ship into the city. That is to say: We arrived from outside the [Shabbat] boundary after nightfall [so are we permitted to disembark]?

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:14:1.english: And the authorities - One who has creditors.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:17:1.english: To accept them with love - For they atone for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:18:1.hebrew: כשהן מספרים - אפי' יש בהן חיות הרבה שמדברים, אעפ"כ מתין פתאום:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:18:1.english: While they are conversing - Even if they have much vitality, such that they are speaking, nevertheless they die suddenly.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:18:2.english: Hidrokan - A disease of the mouth, [in Old French:] musge [thrush].

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:1:1.english: For if it should enter your mind [that it was] regarding all of them - Rav Yehuda stated it.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:1:2.hebrew: הא בעי מיניה רבה מרב יהודה - כדאמרינן לעיל: אתא לקמיה דרב יהודה, ולא הוה בידיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:1:2.english: Didn’t Rabba raise a dilemma before Rav Yehuda - As we said above: He came before Rav Yehuda, and he did not have [an answer] at hand.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:21:1.hebrew: חזר לדעת - מי שהוציאוהו נכרים, וחזר לדעת לתוך התחום — לא הוי כהחזירוהו, דתנן במתני' "כאילו לא יצא":
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:21:1.english: He returned knowingly - [In the case of] one whom gentiles took out and who returned knowingly into the [Shabbat] limit, it is not like [a case where] they returned him, as we learned in the Mishnah: "It is as if he did not go out."

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:25:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - מתני' לצדדין קתני, והחזירוהו דסיפא מילתא באפי נפשה היא, ולאו אהוציאוהו נכרים קאי. והכי קאמר: מי שהוציאוהו נכרים — בין כשהוא עומד בחוץ, בין שחזר לדעת — אין לו אלא ד' אמות; ומי שהיה חוץ לתחום והחזירוהו נכרים — בין שהיתה יציאתו ראשונה לדעת, בין שלא לדעת אלא באונס — הוי כאילו לא יצא:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:25:1.english: Lest you say - The Mishnah teaches disjunctively, and "and they returned him" in the latter clause is an independent matter, and does not refer back to "gentiles took him out." And this is what it means: One whom gentiles took out — whether while he is standing outside or whether he returned knowingly — has only four cubits; and one who was outside the Shabbat limit and gentiles returned him — whether his initial departure was knowing or unknowing, but rather by compulsion — it is as though he had never left.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:1.hebrew: קמ"ל - ר"נ, דסיפא דמתני' ארישא מהדר:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:1.english: He teaches us - Rav Naḥman [teaches us] that the latter clause of the Mishnah refers back to the first clause.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:2.hebrew: הוצרך לנקביו - זה שהוציאוהו נכרים, מהו לצאת מד' אמותיו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:2.english: Needed to relieve himself - [In the case of] this person whom gentiles took out [beyond the Shabbat limit], what is [the ruling regarding whether he may] go beyond his four cubits?

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:3.hebrew: את לא תעשה שבתורה - לאו דלא תסור (דברים יז), ותחומין נמי דרבנן:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:26:3.english: A negative precept of the Torah - [This refers to] the negative commandment of “You shall not turn aside” (Deuteronomy 17:11); and [the prohibition of Shabbat] boundaries is also Rabbinic.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:27:1.english: If he is clever - [This refers to] this person who needed to relieve himself, and the Sages gave him permission to go out beyond his four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:27:2.hebrew: עייל לתחומא וכיון דעל על - ומותר כאילו לא יצא, דהא ברשות על, ולא גרע מהחזירוהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:27:2.english: He will enter into the [Shabbat] limit, and since he entered, he entered - And he is permitted [to move about] as though he had never left, for behold, he entered with permission, and [this] is no worse than [if gentiles] returned him.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:28:1.hebrew: פירות שיצאו חוץ לתחום וחזרו - ביום טוב לא הפסידו מקומן, וכל העיר להן כד' אמות ויש להן לכל רוח אלפים אמה — אם יו"ט הוא; ואי שבת — מותרין לאכילה במקום שחזרו:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:28:1.english: Produce that was taken out beyond the limit and returned - On a Festival, they have not lost their place, and the entire city is [considered] for them like four cubits, and they have two thousand cubits in every direction — if it is a Festival; and if [it was on] Shabbat, they are permitted for eating in the place to which they returned.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:28:2.english: They were coerced - By the one who took them out:

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:29:1.hebrew: אסורין - לזוז אותן מארבע אמותיהן, ולא לאוכלן, אפי' חזרו, אלא אם כן חזרו שוגגין; אבל מזיד — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:29:1.english: [They are] prohibited - To move them beyond their four cubits, nor to eat them, even [if] they returned, unless they returned unwittingly; but [if returned] intentionally, [they are] not [permitted].

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:2:1.english: One fasts and completes - On Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:2:2.hebrew: הא בעי רבה מרב הונא - לעיל, ולא פשט ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:2:2.english: Didn't Rabba ask Rav Huna - [As mentioned] above, and he did not resolve it for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:30:1.english: This is the version we read: It is a dispute between tanna’im, as it was taught: Produce that was taken out beyond the Shabbat limit, unwittingly it may be eaten - And we do not read here: “And returned.”

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:30:2.hebrew: בשוגג יאכלו - במקום שהן שם, אם יש אדם שעירב לאותו צד, או שהיו בני עיר אחרת סמוכים להן:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:30:2.english: [If] unwittingly, they may be eaten - In the place where they are [located], if there is a person who established an eruv in that direction, or if the residents of another town were adjacent to them.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:3:1.hebrew: לבתר דשמעה - רב הונא מרב להאי אבל חכמים אומרים, הדר אגמריה למר זוטרא; ומקמיה דלישמעיה, בעא רבה מיניה ולא פשט ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:3:1.english: After he heard it - [After] Rav Huna [heard] this [teaching of] “but the Sages say” from Rav, he then taught it to Mar Zutra; and before he heard it, Rabba asked him and he did not resolve it for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:3:2.english: Here, too - [The question] regarding Rav Yehuda should not pose a difficulty:

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:3:3.english: This was before he heard it - From Rav.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:3:4.english: This [was] after he heard it - Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda were students of Rav.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:6:1.english: One whom gentiles took out - Outside the [Shabbat] limit.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:6:2.hebrew: או רוח רעה - שנכנס בו שד ונטרפה דעתו, ויצא חוץ לתחום, ואחר כך נשתפה, והרי הוא חוץ לתחום:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:6:2.english: Or an evil spirit - That a demon entered him and his mind became deranged, and he went out beyond the [Shabbat] limit, and afterward he regained his sanity, and behold, he is outside the [Shabbat] limit:

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:7:1.english: [If] they returned him - Into the [Shabbat] limit.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:7:2.hebrew: כאילו לא יצא - והרי כל העיר לו כד' אמות כבתחילה, וחוצה לה אלפים אמה לכל רוח:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:7:2.english: [It is] as though he had not left - And behold, the entire city is [considered] to him as four cubits, as at first, and outside of it [he has] two thousand cubits in every direction.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:8:1.hebrew: הוליכוהו לעיר אחרת - והרי היא מוקפת מחיצות:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:8:1.english: [If] they brought him to another city - And it is surrounded by partitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:8:2.english: Or [if] they put him into a pen or into a stable - For they are enclosed, and their perimeter is large.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:8:3.hebrew: מהלך את כולה - דהואיל ומוקפת מחיצות, הרי היא כד' אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:8:3.english: He may walk about all of it - For since it is surrounded by partitions, it is like four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:1.english: From Pelandarsin - The name of a place.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:2.hebrew: והפליגה - כשהיא מתרחק' משפת הים ונכנסת לאמצעי, קרי ליה הפלגה. ולשון לע"ז הוא, שקורין לשלולית הים פיל"ג:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:2.english: And [their boat] set sail - When it moves away from the shore of the sea and enters into the middle, [the Mishnah] calls it haflaga. And it is an Old French expression, for they call the open sea pelege.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:3.hebrew: הלכו את כולה - היו מהלכין בכל הספינה, דאע"פ שהספינה הולכת בשבת ויצאו חוץ לתחום, הוו כמי שיצא חוץ לתחום וניתן בדיר או בסהר, שהספינה מחיצות לה:
Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:3.english: Walked about the entire [boat] - They walked throughout the entire boat; for even though the boat travels on Shabbat and they went outside the [Shabbat] limit, they are like one who went outside the limit and was placed in a pen or in a corral, as the boat has partitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 41b:9:4.english: As they sought to be stringent - The Gemara explains:

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:14:1.hebrew: הרשות - פי' רבינו חננאל: עול מלכות עובדי כוכבים, כדאמר במסכת אבות (פ"ב מ"ג): "הוו זהירין ברשות". ורש"י פירש: נושה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:14:1.english: "The authorities" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: The yoke of the kingdom of idolaters, as it says in Tractate Avot (2:3): "Be careful with the authorities." And Rashi explained: A creditor.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:25:1.hebrew: לצדדין קתני - אחזר לדעת לא רצה לתרץ כך: "לצדדין קתני", דסוף סוף אהחזירוהו צ"ל לעולם "לצדדין קתני"; (ועוד) דניחא ליה לפרש שיתקיימו דברי רב נחמן הראשונים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:25:1.english: "It is teaching disjunctively" - Regarding [the objection against] "he returned knowingly," [the Gemara] did not want to resolve [it] in this manner, [by answering that] "it is teaching disjunctively," because ultimately, regarding [the clause] "they returned him," one must in any event say [that] "it is teaching disjunctively"; (and furthermore) because it preferred to explain [it such] that Rav Naḥman's original words would be upheld.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:28:1.hebrew: לא הפסידו את מקומן - אע"ג דהבא מחוץ לתחום אסור למי שנשתלח לו, הני מילי התם, דאיתיה חוץ לתחום; אבל הכא, דהשתא הם במקומן — שרי, אפילו להאי דאפקא. ולא דמי למבשל בשבת במזיד לא יאכל, דהתם הוי איסור דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:28:1.english: They have not lost their place - Even though that which is brought from beyond the [Shabbat] limit is forbidden to the one for whom it was sent, this applies only there, where it is outside the limit; but here, where they are now in their [original] place, it is permitted, even to the one who took it out. And it is not similar to [the rule that] one who cooks on Shabbat intentionally may not eat [it], for there it is a Torah prohibition.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:2:1.hebrew: והלכתא מתענה ומשלים - פירוש: אם ירצה להשלים — דשרי להשלים; דבעיא הוא: אי שרי להשלים אי לא. [ומורי אמר לי בשם ה"ר ידידיה, דאפילו ר' יוסי ל"פ אלא דיכול להשלים; מיהו גם ר' יוסי מודה, אי אינו רוצה להשלים — הרשות בידו, ור' יהודה אמר: אסור להשלים. ואין נ"ל, מדקאמר ר'. יוסי: "אי אתה מודה לי בט' באב שחל להיות באחד בשבת שהוא מתחיל מבע"י?" והתם ע"כ דחייב קאמר; דומיא דהכי, ע"ש דחייב להשלים קאמר] [רש"ל בשם תוס' שאנ"ץ]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:2:1.english: "And the halakha is: One fasts and completes [the fast]" - Explanation: [This means] if he wishes to complete [it, he may do so, meaning] that it is permitted to complete [it], for the dilemma was whether it is permitted to complete [it] or not. [And my teacher told me in the name of the master, Rabbi Yedidyah, that even Rabbi Yose disagrees only [to say] that he is able to complete [it]; however, even Rabbi Yose concedes that if he does not wish to complete [it], he has the option [not to do so], and Rabbi Yehuda said [that it is] forbidden to complete [it]. And it does not appear [correct] to me, since Rabbi Yose says: "Do you not concede to me regarding the Ninth of Av that occurs on Sunday, that one begins [fasting] while it is still day?" And there, of necessity he means that one is obligated [to do so]; similar to this, [on] Shabbat eve he means that one is obligated to complete [the fast].] [Maharshal in the name of the Tosafot of Sens].

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:30:1.hebrew: במזיד לא יאכלו - משמע: לשום אדם לא יאכלו. ואף על גב דהבא בשביל ישראל זה מותר לישראל אחר — כיון שנעשה איסור על ידי ישראל, החמירו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:30:1.english: "[If taken out] intentionally, they may not be eaten" - This implies that they may not be eaten by any person. And even though [produce] that was brought for the sake of this Jew is permitted to another Jew, since a prohibition was committed by a Jew, they were stringent.

Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:6:1.hebrew: מי שהוציאוהו. על דעתו ועל דעת קונו - ואע"ג דאיכא נמי כשפים שמכחישין פמליא של מעלה, נראה דהוי בכלל רוח רעה. ויצר הרע — אע"ג דמשמע בפ' ואלו מגלחין (מו"ק ד' יז.) דפעמים שיצרו מתגבר עליו ואינו יכול לכופו, מ"מ אדם יכול ליזהר שלא יבא לידי כך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 41b:6:1.english: "One whom [gentiles] took out" — "Against his will and the will of his Maker" - And even though there is also sorcery, which contradicts the Heavenly retinue, it appears that it is included in [the category of] an evil spirit. And [as for] the evil inclination — even though it is implied in the chapter [entitled] Ve’elu Megalchin (Moed Katan 17a) that at times one's inclination overpowers him and he is unable to suppress it, nevertheless, a person can be careful that he not come to such [a state].
